name: Louisville
title: Investor Renovation Contractor in Louisville, KY | Genstone
metaDescription: Louisville renovation contractor for investors: shotguns, camelbacks, Old Louisville conversions, South End ranches, 203(k) and REO across Jefferson County.
intro:
Louisville has one of the most distinctive investor housing stocks in the country. Long, narrow shotgun houses and camelbacks line the streets of Germantown, Schnitzelburg, Portland and Shelby Park. Old Louisville holds blocks of Victorian mansions, many of them carved into apartments. The Highlands, Crescent Hill and Clifton are full of bungalows and foursquares, and the South End and southwest suburbs stretch out in brick ranches and Cape Cods. Each of those types fails in its own predictable ways, and a renovation budget should be built around them.

Genstone Construction scopes and manages renovations for investors and lenders across Jefferson County: flippers restoring shotguns near the urban core, BRRRR and rental investors in Beechmont, Iroquois and Okolona, small multifamily owners with doubles and converted Victorians, FHA 203(k) buyers and servicers holding bank-owned homes in the West End and beyond. Every project starts with a free Pre-Offer Rehab Review. A designated field manager then runs the job with vetted, licensed Louisville-area contractors and releases draws only for work that is done.
housingStock:
The shotgun house is Louisville's signature investor property. One room wide and several rooms deep, these frame and brick houses were built by the thousands from the late 1800s into the early 1900s for workers in Germantown, Schnitzelburg, Butchertown, Portland, Shelby Park, Smoketown, California and the West End. Camelbacks add a second story at the rear, and double shotguns put two units side by side under one roof. They usually sit on brick piers or low brick foundations over crawlspaces, with tight side yards and alley access.

Old Louisville, south of downtown, is one of the largest Victorian neighborhoods in the United States, with Richardsonian Romanesque, Queen Anne, Italianate and Châteauesque homes built of brick and stone. Many were converted to apartments as the area changed in the twentieth century. The West End's Russell, Shawnee, Parkland and Chickasaw neighborhoods also have substantial brick homes from the same era alongside smaller frame houses.

The Highlands, Cherokee Triangle, Crescent Hill and Clifton developed with streetcar lines in the late 1800s and early 1900s, producing bungalows, foursquares and larger revival-style homes, often with full basements. After the Second World War, Louisville expanded south and southwest into Beechmont, Iroquois, Okolona, Pleasure Ridge Park, Valley Station and Fern Creek with brick ranches, Cape Cods and split-levels.

For a rehab, the age split shapes the scope. Prewar houses commonly carry knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized supply lines, cast-iron and clay drains, lead paint, settling piers and crawlspaces with moisture and termite damage. Old Louisville conversions add fire separation, egress and shared-utility problems. Post-war houses are simpler but bring asbestos floor tile, original panels, aging ductwork and the occasional slab or block foundation issue. Across all eras, Louisville's humid summers and clay soils make moisture control part of almost every job.

commonIssues.title: Sagging floors and settled piers in shotguns
commonIssues.body: Shotgun houses rest on brick piers or short brick foundation walls, and a century of moisture, termites and soil movement often leaves floors sloping toward the middle or rear. Sill beams and joists can be rotted where gutters dumped water against the house. Leveling a shotgun usually means jacking, sistering or replacing joists and sills, rebuilding piers on proper footings and fixing drainage. We price structural work before kitchens and baths, because finishes installed on a moving floor crack within a season.

commonIssues.title: Basement backups in the combined sewer area
commonIssues.body: Much of Louisville's older urban core is served by combined sewers operated by the Metropolitan Sewer District, which carry storm water and sewage in the same pipe. During heavy rain, those lines can surcharge and push water up through basement floor drains. MSD has spent years on overflow projects and has offered programs to help some property owners install backflow prevention. We check for backup history in older basements and price backwater valves, downspout disconnection and lateral repairs when the risk is real.

commonIssues.title: Termites and damp crawlspaces
commonIssues.body: Louisville's warm, humid climate gives subterranean termites a long active season. Shotgun houses, camelbacks and older bungalows with wood near the soil and poorly ventilated crawlspaces are frequent targets. Damage often hides in sill beams, floor joists, door frames and rear additions. We look for mud tubes, soft wood and standing moisture during the walkthrough, and the scope may include treatment coordination, structural repairs, vapor barriers and drainage corrections so the damage does not continue after the renovation.

commonIssues.title: Unpermitted conversions in Old Louisville
commonIssues.body: Many Old Louisville mansions and large West End homes were divided into apartments over decades, sometimes without permits. Common findings include more units than records support, rear units reached by one exterior stair, missing fire separation, shared meters, undersized electrical service and attic apartments with low ceilings. Before buying, confirm the legal unit count with Louisville Metro records. We price the work needed to legitimize units, reduce the count or restore the house to single-family use so you can compare outcomes.

commonIssues.title: Floodplain and creek-side lots
commonIssues.body: Louisville is protected from the Ohio River by a long floodwall and levee system built after the 1937 flood, but low-lying parts of the city near the river, Beargrass Creek and other streams remain in mapped floodplains. Flood status affects insurance, resale and whether a substantial renovation triggers floodplain requirements. We check every parcel near the river or a creek before scoping work, so the budget reflects both construction requirements and long-term holding costs.

investorMarket:
Louisville's flip activity is strongest where owner-occupants are paying for character close to the city's restaurants, parks and employers. Germantown, Schnitzelburg, Shelby Park, Butchertown, the Highlands, Crescent Hill, Clifton and Audubon Park attract buyers who want restored shotguns, camelbacks, bungalows and foursquares with modern systems. In those neighborhoods, well-executed renovations can support quality finishes and careful exterior restoration.

The South End and southwest suburbs, including Beechmont, Iroquois, Wilder Park, Okolona, Pleasure Ridge Park and Valley Station, are buy-and-hold territory. Brick ranches and modest bungalows there rent steadily and appraise predictably, which makes them good candidates for single-family rentals and BRRRR projects.

Old Louisville has a large share of converted multifamily buildings and is close to the University of Louisville, so it draws investors interested in apartments, student and staff rentals and restoration projects. The legal unit count and historic district review need careful attention.

The West End, including Portland, Shawnee, Russell, Chickasaw and Parkland, has lower purchase prices and a large inventory of older homes, including vacant and bank-owned properties. Some investors buy there for long-term rentals, while others focus on blocks seeing new investment. Renovation costs can be high relative to resale values, so underwriting has to be disciplined. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review compares realistic repair costs with nearby values and rents before you buy.
permits:
Louisville Metro Government handles building permits and inspections for most of Jefferson County, including structural work, foundation repair, additions, decks and porches, demolition and many roofing and mechanical projects. A number of small incorporated cities within the county, such as St. Matthews, Shively and Jeffersontown, keep some of their own requirements, so the parcel's jurisdiction should be confirmed early. Kentucky licenses electricians, plumbers and HVAC contractors through the state Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction, and plumbing and electrical work can involve state-level permitting and inspection separate from the building permit.

Louisville Metro's Department of Codes and Regulations enforces property maintenance standards and handles vacant and unsafe structures, so open citations and liens should be checked before purchase. Exterior work in local preservation districts, including Old Louisville, Butchertown, Cherokee Triangle, Clifton and Limerick, generally needs review by Louisville Metro's landmarks staff or the Landmarks Commission before it begins, which affects windows, porches, siding, roofing and masonry. Our field managers sort out which offices apply, pull the permits, schedule inspections and collect lien waivers from every trade.
climate: Louisville sits in a humid, river-valley climate with long, hot summers and winters that swing between mild spells and hard freezes. Summer humidity drives crawlspace moisture, mold, termite activity and heavy air conditioning use, and it slows paint and drywall drying in houses without working HVAC. Winter brings occasional ice storms, which can bring down limbs and damage roofs, gutters and service drops, along with freeze-thaw cycles that loosen brick and mortar. Spring is severe weather season, with heavy rain, hail and tornado risk, and it is when wet basements and roof leaks show themselves. We schedule masonry, roofing and exterior paint for the drier stretches of late spring and fall, and keep interior trades working year-round once power, water and climate control are in place.

faqs.q: Do you work in Southern Indiana as well as Louisville?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Louisville investors also buy across the river in Jeffersonville, New Albany and Clarksville, and we coordinate renovations there too, along with Shepherdsville, Mount Washington, St. Matthews, Shively and Jeffersontown. Indiana and Kentucky have different licensing and permitting systems, and individual cities have their own offices, so your field manager confirms the right jurisdiction for each address before work is scheduled.

faqs.q: What should I check before buying a Louisville shotgun house?
faqs.a: Start with the structure. Look at floor slope, sill beams, piers, crawlspace moisture and termite damage, because those items drive the budget more than kitchens or baths. Then check wiring, supply lines, the sewer lateral and the roof. Confirm whether the property is in a local preservation district, since exterior changes may need review. The free Pre-Offer Rehab Review covers all of this before you commit capital to the purchase.

faqs.q: Is Old Louisville a good place to buy a multifamily property?
faqs.a: It can be, but it is not a simple market. Many buildings have been divided into apartments, and some have more units than records support. Fire separation, egress, utility separation and historic review all affect the renovation. We help investors confirm the likely scope and compare options, including keeping the units, reducing the count or restoring a single-family home, before they decide whether the building fits their goals.

faqs.q: Can I manage a Louisville renovation from out of state?
faqs.a: Yes. Many of our Louisville clients invest from other states. Your field manager walks the property, sends the written scope with photos, posts progress and milestone documentation, and requests draws only after each stage is complete. You review and approve the finished work before final billing. That gives you a clear view of the project without regular trips to Jefferson County or a separate local representative.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in Louisville, KY | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: Louisville fix and flip renovations for shotguns, camelbacks and bungalows in Germantown, Schnitzelburg, the Highlands and Crescent Hill, scoped to local comps.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in Louisville
fix-flip.intro: The classic Louisville flip is a tired shotgun or camelback in Germantown, Schnitzelburg or Shelby Park, or a bungalow in the Highlands, Crescent Hill or Clifton, renovated for a buyer who wants character and a short drive to Bardstown Road or downtown. Those buyers will pay for a well-done house, but they also hire inspectors who crawl under shotguns and know what sagging joists, termite damage and knob-and-tube look like. Genstone Construction builds Louisville flip scopes that start under the floor and work up. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices structure and systems first and then sizes the finish package to recent sales on that street. A designated field manager keeps trades sequenced, coordinates Louisville Metro and state permits, and ties every draw to completed work.

sections.h2: Making a Louisville shotgun feel like a modern home
sections.body:
A shotgun's layout is its biggest selling point and its biggest challenge. Buyers love the tall ceilings, long sightlines and original details, but a string of rooms with no hallway can feel awkward for modern living. The best Louisville shotgun flips open the front rooms into a living area, place a functional kitchen in the middle or rear, and create a bath and bedroom arrangement that provides some privacy, often with a second bath in a camelback's upper story.

We plan those layouts around the structure rather than fighting it. Removing walls in a shotgun can mean adding beams and new support below, and moving a kitchen often means new drain runs in a shallow crawlspace. On exteriors, buyers in Germantown and Schnitzelburg respond to restored front porches, original-style siding and trim, and well-proportioned windows. When the house is inside a preservation district such as Butchertown, those choices also need to fit the district guidelines. We price two finish levels when the comps support it, each with its own ARV estimate, so you can choose.

sections.h2: Structure and systems that Louisville inspectors look for
sections.body:
Louisville buyers' inspectors spend a lot of time under shotguns and in Highlands basements, and the reports they write can unravel a sale. Common findings include sloping floors from failed piers or rotted sills, termite damage in beams and door frames, knob-and-tube wiring tied into later circuits, galvanized supply lines with poor pressure, cast-iron drains cracked along the bottom and clay sewer laterals full of roots.

Those line items come first in the estimate, ahead of any finish selections. A typical urban-core flip scope includes leveling and structural repair under the house, a modern electrical service and wiring, new supply plumbing, drain replacement as needed, a camera inspection of the lateral and repair or lining where it is damaged, a properly sized HVAC system and a roof with sound flashing at chimneys and party walls. In older basements in the combined-sewer area, a backwater valve and downspout corrections may be worth adding. Lead-safe practices apply to windows, trim and porch work on pre-1978 homes. That work produces a clean inspection report, which protects your sale price.

sections.h2: Controlling time and holding costs on a Louisville flip
sections.body:
Holding costs add up quickly when a flip waits for a permit, a historic review or a back-ordered window package. We plan around those bottlenecks from the beginning. Building permits are submitted to Louisville Metro as soon as the scope is approved, and state-licensed electrical, plumbing and HVAC trades handle their own permits and inspections on a schedule that keeps the job moving. Long-lead materials are ordered from the approved scope rather than after demolition.

If the house is in Butchertown, Cherokee Triangle, Clifton, Limerick or another local preservation district, we put the exterior plans in front of Louisville Metro's landmarks staff early, because changes to windows, porches or siding may need approval before work starts. Weather matters too: we push masonry, roofing and exterior paint into dry stretches, avoiding the wettest spring weeks and the hottest summer afternoons. Your field manager posts progress so you can line up your listing agent, photographer and staging around a realistic finish date, and draws follow completed work.

faqs.q: Which Louisville neighborhoods are best for flips?
faqs.a: Germantown, Schnitzelburg, Shelby Park, Butchertown, the Highlands, Crescent Hill, Clifton and Audubon Park tend to have the strongest owner-occupant demand for renovated older homes. Parts of the South End can also work for ranches and bungalows at a lower price point. Demand changes block by block, so we look at recent sales on the specific street during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review before recommending a scope.

faqs.q: How much structural work should I expect in a Louisville shotgun?
faqs.a: It varies, but most century-old shotguns need some leveling, pier rebuilding or joist and sill repair, especially near the rear where additions and old porches were enclosed. Termite damage is common. We inspect the crawlspace during the walkthrough and price structural work as its own line items, so you can see exactly how much of the budget goes under the floor before any finishes.

faqs.q: Can you add a second bathroom to a camelback or shotgun?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Camelbacks have room upstairs for a second bath, and longer shotguns can sometimes fit one off the rear bedroom. The challenge is plumbing: drains need proper slope in a shallow crawlspace and vents must be routed correctly. We review layout and plumbing feasibility during the walkthrough and price the bath only if it makes sense for the comps.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in Louisville, KY | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: BRRRR renovations in Louisville: South End ranches, Beechmont and Iroquois bungalows and West End homes rehabbed for refinance appraisals and long-term tenants.
brrrr.intro: Louisville BRRRR investors tend to work the South End and southwest suburbs, where brick ranches and modest bungalows in Beechmont, Iroquois, Wilder Park, Okolona and Pleasure Ridge Park can be bought below the value of renovated comparables and rented steadily. Some also buy shotguns and larger older homes in the West End and Portland, where purchase prices are lower but appraisals and renovation costs need closer scrutiny. Genstone Construction plans Louisville BRRRR projects to meet the refinance appraisal while building a durable rental. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review estimates the renovation and checks it against likely post-repair value so you can see whether the refinance will return enough of your capital. Genstone Financial, a sister company, offers DSCR rental loans for investors who want the refinance coordinated with the rehab.

sections.h2: Renovating South End homes to the refinance appraisal
sections.body:
An appraiser in Jefferson County values a renovated rental against recent sales of comparable houses, so the scope should match the better-maintained homes on that street and stop there. For a 1950s brick ranch in Okolona or Pleasure Ridge Park, that usually means a sound roof, updated electrical panel, working furnace and central air, a clean kitchen with durable counters, a refreshed bath, consistent hard-surface flooring and fresh paint. For a 1920s bungalow in Beechmont or Iroquois, add the plumbing and wiring updates older houses usually need.

Items that rarely move an appraisal in these neighborhoods include high-end tile, custom cabinetry and elaborate landscaping. Items that do matter include functioning systems, an absence of deferred maintenance, a dry crawlspace or basement and a clean, updated kitchen and bath. We document every upgrade with dated photos, permits and an itemized list of replaced systems so the appraiser can see what changed. That record carries extra weight when the online listing still shows the house before renovation.

After the refinance, the house has to hold up as a rental through hot summers, ice storms and tenant turnover. Air conditioning in Louisville runs hard from late spring into fall, so we size and install HVAC equipment for that load and make sure ductwork is sealed and returns are adequate. Crawlspaces get vapor barriers, drainage corrections and termite inspections because moisture problems there lead to mold, sagging floors and odors that drive tenants away.

Inside, we favor luxury vinyl plank in kitchens, baths and living areas, standardized paint colors and sheens, durable counters and fixtures that a maintenance tech can replace from local stock. Gutters and downspouts are repaired and extended to move water away from foundations. In older homes in the combined-sewer area, backwater valves and downspout disconnection can prevent the kind of basement backup that ruins tenant belongings. For pre-1978 homes, lead-safe practices apply, and owners leasing to households with housing assistance should expect lead-related inspections. Simple, dry and sturdy rentals keep more of their cash flow.

Not every inexpensive Louisville house is a good BRRRR candidate. The strongest ones are structurally sound homes in neighborhoods with steady rental demand and enough recent retail sales to support the refinance. Brick ranches in the South End and southwest suburbs often fit because their structure is straightforward and their comps are predictable.

Shotguns and older West End homes can work but carry heavier risk. Sagging floors, termite-damaged sills and piers, knob-and-tube wiring and old laterals add up quickly, and in blocks with few renovated sales the appraisal may not reflect the work. Converted homes in Old Louisville may have unpermitted units, egress problems and historic review requirements that complicate both the rehab and the refinance. Properties near Beargrass Creek or other low areas need a floodplain check, since flood insurance can shrink cash flow.

We flag those risks during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review. If a property does not fit BRRRR, we may suggest a lighter rental renovation or a longer hold, and sometimes the best advice is to pass on the deal.

faqs.q: Can Genstone coordinate the refinance on a Louisville BRRRR?
faqs.a: We handle the renovation, and Genstone Financial, a separate company within the Genstone Companies, provides DSCR rental loans, fix-and-flip loans and lines of credit. You can use any lender. If you want the renovation documentation and the refinance working together from the start, we can introduce you to Genstone Financial before you close on the Louisville property, so the loan is sized around a realistic scope.

faqs.q: What Louisville properties work best for BRRRR?
faqs.a: Structurally sound homes in areas with steady rental demand and good comps tend to work best. Brick ranches and bungalows in Beechmont, Iroquois, Wilder Park, Okolona and Pleasure Ridge Park are common choices. Shotguns and older West End homes can work at the right price, but structural and system costs need to be priced carefully during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review before you buy.

faqs.q: Do Louisville rental appraisals give credit for a finished basement?
faqs.a: Sometimes, if the basement is dry, permitted and consistent with comparable homes. Many older Louisville basements take on water or are at risk of sewer backup, and finishing them before solving those problems invites damage and tenant complaints. We address water first, then help you decide whether finishing the space makes sense for the specific street and comps. In many Okolona and Pleasure Ridge Park ranches, there is no basement to finish at all.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in Louisville, KY | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: Single-family rental renovation in Louisville for portfolio owners: consistent specs, humidity-ready HVAC, crawlspace and termite work, and tenant-ready turns.
rental-renovation.intro: A Louisville rental portfolio rarely sticks to one kind of house. An owner might hold a shotgun in Portland, a brick ranch in Okolona, a bungalow in Beechmont and a newer two-story in Fern Creek, each with different structure and systems. The renovation challenge is creating a consistent standard across that mix while respecting what each house needs. Genstone Construction renovates single-family rentals across Louisville and Jefferson County for individual investors, funds and portfolio operators. We handle initial stabilization when you acquire a property, renovations between long-term tenants and ongoing turn work through our sister company Genstone Field Services. Each job has a designated field manager, itemized pricing and photo documentation, so you can oversee the portfolio from anywhere.

sections.h2: A Louisville rental standard that works across eras
sections.body:
Consistency in finishes saves money over the life of a portfolio. Flooring, paint colors and sheens, cabinet lines, counters, plumbing fixtures, lighting and appliance packages can be identical in a Portland shotgun and an Okolona ranch. That simplifies purchasing, speeds up turns and makes repairs easier for maintenance techs.

Structure and systems are different. A shotgun may need floor leveling, pier work, termite repair, rewiring and a new sewer lateral. A 1950s ranch may need a new panel, furnace, condenser and water heater. A 1990s house may need little more than mechanical servicing and cosmetic updates. We write those differences into each scope so the per-door budget reflects real conditions, and so the property manager inherits a house without hidden problems behind fresh paint.

The standard should also include Louisville-specific durability items: properly sized air conditioning, sealed ductwork, crawlspace vapor barriers, gutters and downspouts that move water away from the house and, in older urban-core homes, backwater protection where sewer backups are a risk.

sections.h2: Keeping Louisville rentals dry, cool and termite-free
sections.body:
Humidity is the long-term enemy of Louisville rental houses. Damp crawlspaces and basements lead to mold, musty odors, sagging floors and termite activity, while poor attic ventilation shortens roof life and raises cooling bills. During renovation, we trace the full water path: roof drainage, gutters, grading, plumbing leaks, crawlspace ventilation and vapor barriers. Where moisture is persistent, dehumidification or encapsulation may be worth the cost.

Termite damage shows up regularly in older homes, especially shotguns and bungalows with wood close to the soil. We look for activity during scoping and include treatment coordination and structural repair as needed.

Air conditioning is a retention issue as much as a comfort issue. Tenants in older homes with undersized or failing systems complain all summer and leave at lease end. We size equipment for the house, seal ducts and make sure condensate lines drain properly. For owners renting to households with housing assistance, working heat and cooling, smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, safe stairs and lead-safe conditions are also central to passing inspections.

sections.h2: Turns and make-ready across a Louisville portfolio
sections.body:
After stabilization, the recurring job is getting each Louisville house back on the market between residents. Genstone Field Services, part of the Genstone Companies, provides turn and make-ready work, inspections and occupied maintenance, so the same organization that renovated the house can keep it ready for the next resident.

For Louisville owners, a turn means a photographed move-out inspection, a written scope priced against your standard and repairs by vetted Jefferson County contractors. Because the renovation used standard materials, matching flooring, paint and fixtures is straightforward. Photos of damage support deposit decisions and build a history of each property's condition.

We also use turns to check the items that cause trouble in this climate: HVAC filters and condensate drains, crawlspace moisture, gutters and signs of termite activity. Catching a small leak or a clogged drain line between tenants is far cheaper than repairing water damage mid-lease. Genstone's one-year workmanship warranty covers the work we performed, while tenant damage and normal wear are part of the turn scope. Your property manager can coordinate access and resident communication while you follow approvals and progress remotely.

faqs.q: Can you renovate Louisville rentals while tenants live there?
faqs.a: Yes. Occupied work is scheduled with notice, confined to defined areas and planned so residents keep a working kitchen, bath and climate control whenever possible. In the hottest weeks of summer, air conditioning work is scheduled to keep downtime short, with the new unit on site before the old one is pulled. Genstone Field Services also handles occupied maintenance, so smaller repairs between renovations do not require a separate vendor.

faqs.q: Do you coordinate with Louisville property management companies?
faqs.a: Yes. We can take access requests and resident questions through your property manager while sending you scopes, photos and approval requests directly. You choose who approves changes, and anything outside the approved scope waits for that approval before it is billed. That arrangement suits owners who live outside Kentucky and rely on a manager for local contact with residents, and it keeps tenants from fielding calls from several directions.

faqs.q: How do you price rental renovations across many Louisville homes?
faqs.a: Each property gets its own itemized estimate, with finishes and many line items drawn from your portfolio standard so costs are consistent and easy to compare. Structural and system work is priced house by house, so you can see why a Portland shotgun costs more than an Okolona ranch. Haul-off and dumpsters are built into each estimate, and payment is released as each stage is finished.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & 2-4 Unit Renovation in Louisville, KY | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: Louisville small multifamily renovation: double shotguns, Old Louisville conversions and fourplexes, with fire separation, egress, split utilities and phasing.
multifamily-renovation.intro: Louisville's small multifamily stock is unusually varied. Double shotguns put two narrow units side by side under one roof in Germantown, Portland and Shelby Park. Old Louisville and parts of the West End are full of Victorian mansions divided into three, four or more apartments. The Highlands and Crescent Hill have brick fourplexes and up-and-down duplexes from the streetcar era, and the suburbs add post-war duplexes. Genstone Construction renovates two- to four-unit properties across Louisville for investors who want several rents under one roof. We focus on the parts that make these buildings harder than single-family homes: legal unit count, fire separation, egress, shared utilities and phasing around occupied units. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices that work before you buy.

sections.body:
A double shotgun is two long, narrow units sharing a center wall, a roof and often a crawlspace. They are popular with Louisville investors because they offer two rents on one narrow lot, and in strong neighborhoods some are converted to a single wide house for resale. The challenges are structural and mechanical: shared piers and sills that have settled, a party wall that may not provide real fire separation, a single water service and sometimes a single electrical service split with a subpanel.

For a rental, separate electric and gas meters and independent HVAC for each side let tenants pay their own utilities and control their own comfort. We coordinate new services with LG&E, size panels for modern loads and route ductwork through tight crawlspaces and attics.

Brick fourplexes in the Highlands and Crescent Hill are typically sturdier but often have original boilers, shared laundry, worn stairways and electrical systems that were modified piecemeal. We evaluate whether to keep a central boiler or convert to individual systems, because that choice affects the whole renovation budget.

sections.h2: Old Louisville conversions: unit count, egress and review
sections.body:
Old Louisville's large Victorians were divided into apartments over decades, and quality varies widely. Some conversions were permitted and well executed, while others added units without permits. Common problems include rear units reached only by one exterior stair, attic units with low ceilings, basement units with small windows, missing fire separation between floors and electrical services overloaded by several kitchens.

Before buying, confirm the legal unit count through Louisville Metro records and compare it with the building as it stands. From there, the renovation can bring existing units up to current requirements, reduce the unit count to something that can be legitimized and financed, or restore a single-family home where buyer demand supports it. We price those paths side by side.

Old Louisville is a local preservation district, so exterior work such as new fire stairs, window replacement, porch repair and masonry generally needs review by Louisville Metro's landmarks staff or the Landmarks Commission. Interior safety work usually proceeds without that review. We build both into the schedule so neither surprises you midway through the project.

Many Louisville multifamily buyers inherit tenants, and their rent helps carry the building while vacant units are renovated. We phase work to protect that income: vacant units first, then occupied units as leases end or as tenants move into finished units.

Whole-building items, such as a new roof, electrical service upgrade, gas line replacement, sewer lateral repair or boiler replacement, are scheduled with advance notice and kept as short as possible. In summer, occupied units need cooling; in winter, heat stays on. Shared hallways, stairs and basements are cleaned and secured daily so residents are not living next to an open job site.

Your field manager coordinates resident notices through your property manager if you have one, photographs each phase and closes permits and inspections before the next stage begins. That keeps the building producing income while it improves and leaves you with a documented record for lenders and insurers. On a double shotgun, it can mean finishing one side completely and leasing it before starting the other.

faqs.q: Should I keep a Louisville double shotgun as two units or convert it?
faqs.a: It depends on the neighborhood. In Germantown, Schnitzelburg and parts of the Highlands, a converted double can sell well to owner-occupants who want more width and space. Where rents are strong and resale demand is thinner, keeping two units usually performs better. Zoning, structural condition and conversion costs all matter, and we price both paths during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so you can compare them.

faqs.q: How do I confirm the legal unit count in an Old Louisville building?
faqs.a: Start with Louisville Metro permit and zoning records and compare them with the current layout. Property valuation records and older listings help but are not definitive. If the records support fewer units than exist, we can price the work to legitimize them where zoning allows, or a plan to reduce the count. Knowing this before purchase protects both your budget and your financing options.

faqs.q: Is it worth separating utilities in a Louisville duplex?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Separate electric and gas meters and independent HVAC let tenants pay their own utilities and control their own comfort, which reduces disputes and owner expense. The cost includes new services, panels and equipment, so it has to be weighed against rents. We price separation as its own line item so you can see the effect on your numbers before deciding.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in Louisville, KY | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) certified contractor in Louisville: Standard and Limited bids for shotguns, bungalows, ranches and owner-occupied doubles, with consultant support.
fha-203k.intro: Louisville's housing stock is full of homes that make sense for a 203(k) buyer: a shotgun in Schnitzelburg with sloping floors and old wiring, a Beechmont bungalow with a failing roof, a South End ranch with a dead furnace and peeling paint. Those homes often will not pass a standard FHA appraisal as-is, but they can become good owner-occupied houses with the right renovation. A 203(k) loan finances the purchase and repairs together. As an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, Genstone writes the itemized bids, scopes and draw schedules that Louisville lenders and consultants work from, and then manages the renovation through completion. Buyers, agents and loan officers rely on that paperwork discipline to keep renovation loans from stalling between contract and closing.

sections.h2: Standard or Limited 203(k) for a Louisville home
sections.body:
For lighter, nonstructural work, the Limited 203(k) caps total rehabilitation costs at $75,000. Projects above $15,000 require an inspection, while smaller ones leave that decision to the lender. A consultant is optional on Limited loans, though some lenders require one. In Louisville, the Limited version suits a South End ranch that needs a furnace and condenser, roof, flooring and a kitchen update, or a Beechmont bungalow that needs windows, paint and a bathroom.

The Standard 203(k) is built for bigger and structural projects. Repairs must total at least $5,000, and an FHA-approved 203(k) consultant is part of every Standard loan. It is usually the right fit for a shotgun or camelback that needs floor leveling, pier and sill repair, termite damage correction, a full rewire, new plumbing or a reworked layout. We walk the house with the buyer and agent, explain what we see and recommend the version that matches the real scope. A structural shotgun job squeezed into the Limited program almost always causes delays.

The strongest 203(k) candidates in Louisville are homes whose problems are significant but well defined. Examples include a Germantown shotgun with failing piers and knob-and-tube wiring, a Highlands bungalow with an old boiler and a wet basement, or an Okolona ranch with a dead HVAC system and worn roof.

Crawlspaces and termites deserve early attention because they are common in Louisville's older homes and can change the budget substantially. Basements in the combined-sewer area may need backwater valves and drainage improvements. Homes near Beargrass Creek or the river should be checked for floodplain status, since flood insurance and floodplain rules affect the loan.

FHA also allows owner-occupied properties with two to four units, so a buyer can purchase a double shotgun or small multifamily building, live in one unit and renovate the rest with 203(k) financing. In Old Louisville and other preservation districts, exterior changes may need landmarks review, which should be built into the timeline before closing.

sections.h2: Bids, consultants and draws on Louisville 203(k) loans
sections.body:
Lenders on a 203(k) typically want a detailed bid broken out line by line and matched to the consultant's work write-up, plus our licensing and insurance documentation. We prepare Louisville bids that way and revise them promptly when the appraiser, consultant or underwriter requests changes.

After closing, the renovation funds sit in escrow and are released in stages as inspected work is completed. Our field manager schedules the job so each draw lines up with a clear milestone, collects lien waivers from each trade and coordinates Louisville Metro building permits along with state-licensed electrical, plumbing and HVAC work.

Lead-safe practices are used on pre-1978 homes, which includes most of Louisville's older housing. When hidden conditions surface after demolition, such as termite-eaten sills, rotted joists or a broken lateral, we document them and follow the lender's change-order process so contingency funds are used properly. The homeowner can follow each milestone remotely, and the last payment is released only once the work is finished and they have signed off on it.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) loan cover structural work on a Louisville shotgun?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Standard 203(k), which allows structural repairs and requires an FHA-approved consultant. Floor leveling, pier rebuilding, sill and joist replacement and termite damage correction can all be included in the scope. Because those costs vary a great deal from house to house, we inspect the crawlspace carefully during the walkthrough so the bid and loan amount reflect the real work.

faqs.q: Do you work directly with Louisville lenders and 203(k) consultants?
faqs.a: Yes. Our bids go directly to the loan officer and consultant, and we answer their questions and make revisions without slowing the file down. We keep the buyer's agent informed so the contract dates stay realistic. Getting the contractor, consultant and lender aligned early is the most reliable way to keep a Louisville renovation loan moving toward closing, especially on a shotgun where the structural scope may change after the consultant's visit.

faqs.q: Can I buy a Louisville double shotgun with a 203(k) loan?
faqs.a: Yes, if you will live in one side. FHA allows owner-occupied properties with up to four units, and Louisville doubles are a common choice. The renovation can cover both units, including structural work and utility separation. Your lender will confirm eligibility and how the second unit's rent is counted, and we make sure the scope addresses fire separation between the units.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in Louisville | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: REO renovation in Louisville for servicers, banks and GSEs: termite and moisture damage, mold, stripped systems and Codes and Regulations cases on vacant homes.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovations in Louisville
reo-renovation.intro: Vacant homes deteriorate quickly in Louisville's humid climate. A bank-owned shotgun or South End ranch that sat closed through a summer can come back with mold on the walls, a soaked crawlspace and fresh termite damage, and one that sat through an ice storm or a hard freeze may also have split pipes and roof damage. Theft of copper and HVAC equipment, vandalism and open citations from Louisville Metro Codes and Regulations are common too. Genstone Construction renovates REO properties in Louisville and Jefferson County for mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, which list Genstone as a preferred contractor. Through our sister company Genstone Field Services, the same organization can secure, winterize, inspect and clear code issues before and during the renovation.

sections.h2: Conditions common in vacant Louisville homes
sections.body:
Moisture is the first thing we look for in a Louisville REO. A closed house with no air conditioning traps summer humidity, and mold can spread across walls, cabinets and ceilings in a single season. Crawlspaces under shotguns and bungalows stay damp, which softens sills and joists and draws termites. Roof leaks from storms or ice can go unnoticed for months and soak insulation and drywall below.

Theft and vandalism follow vacancy, especially in the West End, Portland and parts of the South End. Copper supply lines, condensers, furnaces and water heaters are frequently missing, and broken windows and forced doors let weather and trespassers in. Basements in the older core may show evidence of sewer backups from the combined system.

We start each assignment with a full walkthrough, photographs of every room, the crawlspace and the attic, and a pressure test on any remaining plumbing. Missing systems are listed for replacement. We also confirm utility status, since LG&E and Louisville Water may need repairs and inspections completed before service is restored.

sections.h2: Code cases and permits for Louisville REO
sections.body:
Louisville Metro's Department of Codes and Regulations cites vacant properties for tall grass, debris, open structures, broken windows and unsafe conditions, and unpaid fines and abatement charges can become liens. Some properties end up on unsafe or demolition lists. When a servicer or bank takes title, those cases come along with it.

Genstone Field Services handles code compliance work and coordinates with Genstone Construction so open citations are corrected as part of the renovation plan. Building permits are pulled through Louisville Metro, while state-licensed electrical, plumbing and HVAC trades handle their own permits and inspections. Each correction is documented and tied to the citation it resolves so the case can be closed.

Properties in Old Louisville, Butchertown, Cherokee Triangle, Clifton, Limerick and other local preservation districts may need landmarks review before exterior repairs, which affects windows, porches and siding. Homes in floodplains near the river or Beargrass Creek can trigger additional requirements when repairs are substantial. We build those steps into the timeline so a property does not stall late in the process.

sections.h2: Louisville REO scopes matched to disposition
sections.body:
Asset managers usually want one of three outcomes: a retail-ready home for an owner-occupant buyer, a property repaired to meet FHA or conventional financing standards, or a limited scope that resolves health, safety and code items before an investor sale. We write scopes to the chosen strategy, with line items that make options easy to compare.

In Louisville, a retail-ready scope often includes restoring water, power and HVAC, mold remediation, crawlspace moisture correction, termite and structural repairs, roof work, new flooring and paint, kitchen and bath updates and exterior cleanup. A financing-focused scope concentrates on what an appraiser will call out, such as peeling paint on a pre-1978 home, missing handrails, inoperable systems or active leaks. A limited scope may secure the property, remove debris, correct hazards and clear citations.

Every estimate includes dumpster and debris costs, and every closeout includes lien waivers and before-and-after photos. A designated field manager stays with each Louisville property from the first walkthrough to final billing, giving asset managers one contact for approvals, status and reporting.

faqs.q: Does Genstone handle preservation and renovation for Louisville REO?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone Field Services provides property preservation, inspections, occupied maintenance, turn and make-ready work and code compliance, and Genstone Construction completes the renovation. Keeping both within the Genstone Companies means one photo history and one set of records for each Louisville address, from the first lock change through the finished rehab, which simplifies reporting for servicers managing many assets across Jefferson County.

faqs.q: How do you deal with mold and termites in vacant Louisville homes?
faqs.a: We find the moisture source first, whether it is a roof leak, failed plumbing, crawlspace humidity or poor drainage, and correct it. Affected materials are then remediated. Termite activity is documented, treatment is coordinated and damaged framing is repaired or replaced. Running dehumidification or HVAC during the listing period helps keep the house from sliding back after the work is done.

faqs.q: Can you clear Codes and Regulations citations on bank-owned homes?
faqs.a: Yes. We review open citations with the asset manager, include the corrective work in the scope, pull the necessary permits and provide documentation so each case can be closed. Exterior items such as mowing, debris removal, boarding and broken glass are usually handled first, which helps prevent new complaints and fines while interior repairs move forward. If a property appears on a demolition list, we notify the asset manager right away.
